title: MEL-Code: Transferring Meta-Experience Learning to Code RLVR with Unit-Test Rewards

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to enable Meta-Experience Learning (MEL), previously limited to mathematical reasoning, to work in code generation RLVR where solutions may differ from the first line. Paper [1] discusses the meta-learning bottleneck in RLVR and the need for mechanisms for error attribution and experience internalization, which aligns with the broader goal of enabling MEL in RLVR. However, [1] does not specifically address the extension of MEL to the code generation domain or the challenge of handling solutions that differ from the first line. None of the other papers explicitly address this purpose either. Therefore, no prior paper fully covers this purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves a three-stage pipeline: (1) contrastive pair construction from GRPO rollouts, (2) replay validation via unit-test re-execution, and (3) NLL internalization with template-based meta-experience construction suited to the code domain. Paper [16] discusses automatic pair construction for contrastive post-training, which aligns with the first stage of the pipeline. Paper [9] uses unit-test pass rates as a reward signal, which is conceptually similar to replay validation via unit-test re-execution. However, neither [16] nor [9] combines these elements into a three-stage pipeline or applies them specifically to meta-experience construction in the code domain. Thus, while individual components of the mechanism are partially covered, the full mechanism is not substantively equivalent to any prior work.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with MBPP training, achieving the highest MBPP performance and 33% faster convergence than baselines. Paper [13] introduces Qwen2.5, but it does not evaluate it on MBPP or use the same evaluation design. Paper [9] evaluates code generation using unit-test pass rates, which is a common evaluation design in RLVR for code generation. Since the evaluation design (unit-test-based validation and performance benchmarking) is standard in the field and appears in prior work like [9], the evaluation facet is covered.

### Domain
The domain is code generation with reinforcement learning (RLVR). Papers [2], [3], [4], [6], [7], [8], [9], and [12] all address RLVR for code generation, covering various aspects such as compiler feedback, reasoning-process rewards, and co-evolving coders and unit testers. This establishes that the domain is well-covered by prior work.
